title: Monte Carlo sampling from a projected entangled-pair state in simulations of quantum annealing in the three dimensional random Ising model
summary: Quantum annealing with the D-Wave Advantage system in the random Ising model on a cubic lattice is simulated using a three-dimensional (3D) tensor network. The Hamiltonian is driven across a quantum phase transition from a paramagnetic phase to a spin-glass phase. The network is represented as a tensor product state, also known-particularly in two dimensions-as a projected entangled-pair state (PEPS).
